observation_contract.positive_semantics: Foreground or midground physical entity overlaps the ROI and visibly occludes scene behind it or terminates a central line of sight.
positive_exclusions: object merely visible without material central occlusion
observation_contract.negative_semantics: Forward-looking ROI is reviewable and the positive observation is unsupported; never CLEAR, SAFE, FREE_SPACE, or TRAVERSABLE.
observation_contract.not_evaluable_semantics: Forward-looking ROI unavailable or unreliable because of quality, non-scene content, hard cut, unusable dimensions, near-total occlusion, or camera orientation.

parent_event_rule.definition: Maximal consecutive frozen observations with the same label inside one frozen clip; a continuous NOT_EVALUABLE episode remains one event.

calibration_learning.predecessor_observation: R0 source-only calibration inspection showed that saying any scene element materially occupies the ROI would classify ordinary background architecture as obstruction.
calibration_learning.supported_inference: The positive label needs an occlusion or line-of-sight termination condition, not mere visibility inside the ROI.
alternative_explanations: Some close surfaces remain genuinely ambiguous at the ROI boundary.
Camera turns and edited scene cuts can mimic rapid obstruction transitions.
calibration_learning.information_gained: Foreground/midground occlusion is a better image-observation proxy than generic ROI occupancy.
